clue.text: March across for an easy victory

definitions.meaning: a contest won without opposition, as when a rival fails to turn up

explanation.surface: Soldiers marching over open ground win without a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking over a field and a no-contest win share one phrase; the win is named from a horse walking the course alone.

clue.text: Miss Australian city

definitions.meaning: a woman's name used with the title Miss

explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, famous from the showgirl in Guys and Dolls, is also the capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Light-fingered man police endlessly take off?

indicators.note: off here means set off course or awry, so the gathered letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the word police loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief asks whether police officers will take him away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts POLICE to POLIC; 'off' then shuffles MAN + POLIC + TAKE into the answer, used here as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A compulsive thief is described as light-fingered, given to stealing.

clue.text: State aid for hobos

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
grants are sums of money given as aid

explanation.surface: Public money is handed out to tramps.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobos are homeless wanderers, the American term for tramps.

clue.text: Reportedly studied lovable animals

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: studied gives read and lovable gives dear

explanation.surface: Someone has apparently researched cuddly creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deer species of Europe and Asia is a kind of wild beast.

clue.text: County, it appears, has limited accommodation

parts.note: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county
taken as written

explanation.surface: A county seems short of housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat with a bed in the living space is very cramped lodging.

clue.text: Pulpit used by William Booth

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The founder of the Salvation Army preaches from a raised stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An early Christian church's raised reading desk served as a pulpit.

clue.text: Illustration of fashionable pose

parts.note: in means in fashion
a stance is a posture or pose

explanation.surface: A fashion drawing shows a model's posture.
explanation.definitionFit: An example given to illustrate a point is a case in point.

clue.text: Morality for all of us

definitions.meaning: a morality play, the medieval allegorical drama
the ordinary person, standing for everyone

explanation.surface: Ethics apply to everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval morality play has a title figure who stands for the common person, the representative of humankind.

clue.text: Sound of pet dog

indicators.note: sound of tells the solver to say a word aloud and spell what is heard differently

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in pique

explanation.surface: A dog owner hears the noise their animal makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese is a small toy breed, often shortened.

clue.text: Salaried post arranged for poet's work

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet is offered a paid job.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic of the Fall of Man is a celebrated poem.

clue.text: Very lengthy pine removed from bank

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
money taken out of a bank account is drawn out

explanation.surface: A pine tree is taken away from a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Something protracted is stretched out far beyond its due length.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge one's in the county

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the county's name

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
one is I, and one's gives I'S

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit they are in the county.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown a child is to reject and cut ties with them.

clue.text: Point taken by schoolboy from part of USSR

indicators.note: taken by means the compass point is held inside the schoolboy

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A schoolboy makes a point about the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic republic of Estonia was once a Soviet republic, so its native was Soviet-born.

clue.text: Degenerate Restoration comedy

definitions.meaning: to slip back into a worse state
The ..., the 1696 play by John Vanbrugh

explanation.surface: A bawdy seventeenth-century comedy shows moral decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling back into illness or vice shares its name with Vanbrugh's play of 1696.

clue.text: Being present for change of party allegiance?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: siding again, with a different party

explanation.surface: A politician turns up for a defection.
explanation.definitionFit: Living somewhere means being there; read as a coinage it means taking sides anew.

clue.text: Made changes in outstanding university

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reformed a top-flight university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns MADE into ADEM, which 'in' places inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of scholarship, the academic community of a university.

clue.text: Conceivably, fifty stay up in show of grief

indicators.note: in means the turned pieces are placed within the word for a show of grief

parts.note: a cry is weeping, a show of grief

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the words fifty and stay are read from bottom to top

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to bide is to stay

explanation.surface: Fifty mourners stay on in a display of sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses L + BIDE to EDIBL, and 'in' puts that inside CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Credibly means in a believable way, so plausibly.

clue.text: Lesser burden of blame for islander

parts.note: minor means lesser
the can, as in carry the can, is responsibility for blame

explanation.surface: A minor figure takes the blame for someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry the can is a British idiom for taking the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Menorca, a Balearic island, is a kind of islander.

clue.text: Love following Thomas, the poet

parts.note: the poet's full name runs Thomas, then Love, then the surname wanted

explanation.surface: A poet's love comes after Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Love Peacock was an English poet and satirical novelist.

clue.text: Between Mediterranean islands one turns friendly

indicators.note: turns says the whole run is then read backwards
between means one goes in the middle of the two islands

parts.note: Elba and Cos are both islands in the Mediterranean
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller between islands becomes friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between' sets I between ELBA and COS; 'turns' reverses ELBAICOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable person is convivial, enjoying company.

clue.text: Outstanding specimen observable only in the hide?

definitions.text: Outstanding specimen observable only in the hide?

parts.words: Outstanding specimen observable only in the hide?
parts.note: a fine specimen, and the proverb says this quality lies only skin deep, the hide being skin

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a rare bird only from a hide.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is that good looks are only skin deep; 'hide' suggests a birdwatcher's shelter but means skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunner is an outstanding example, and good looks proverbially lie only on the skin's surface.

clue.text: After chat, she becomes mistress of the house

definitions.text: After chat, she becomes mistress of the house

parts.words: After chat, she becomes mistress of the house
parts.note: a woman's name which, when written after the word chat, makes a word for a woman running a large household

explanation.surface: A gossiping woman takes charge of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: Written after CHAT, the name makes CHATELAINE, the mistress of a great house.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name of Arthurian legend, Lancelot's lover, is a girl's name.

clue.text: in which Mrs Henchard was disposed of?

definitions.text: in which Mrs Henchard was disposed of?

parts.words: in which Mrs Henchard was disposed of?
parts.note: in Hardy's novel the Mayor of Casterbridge, a drunken Henchard sells his wife at a fair, the price dropping as he calls

explanation.surface: A question about how a Hardy heroine was got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: Henchard drops his asking price for his wife until a sailor buys her, like a sale where the price falls until someone bids.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale where the asking price is lowered step by step until a bidder accepts.

clue.text: Choice between two youth leaders for right type

indicators.note: between means the word for choice sits in the middle of the two leading letters
leaders means the first letters of two and youth

parts.note: or expresses a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: Two young candidates contest a right-wing seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Conservative is a person of the political right.

clue.text: Start of fairytale not repeated

definitions.meaning: fairy tales traditionally begin with ... upon a time

explanation.surface: A fairy tale begins without repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-occasion events happen one time; fairy stories open with the same word.

clue.text: Drug Red Cross needed in terrible action

indicators.note: needed in says the abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
terrible signals that the word action is mangled

explanation.surface: Red Cross aid is needed after a dreadful deed involving drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles ACTION into NAOTIC, and 'needed in' puts RC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is an opiate or similar substance that dulls the senses.

clue.text: Sort of cop central to hold-up?

definitions.meaning: the ... Cops, bungling police of silent film comedies
the wedge-shaped stone at the crown of an arch that keeps it standing

explanation.surface: A policeman is at the heart of a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent-film police and the central wedge locking an arch share the name.
